title: The True Value of Wealth
passage:
There was an old woman. She was very rich, but she never spent any of her wealth. Instead, she saved all of her gold in a case. She buried the case in a secret spot in her garden.

Each day, the woman went into her garden. She dug up the hidden case and opened it. Then, she counted the coins one by one. After the woman counted the last coin, she shut the case and buried it once more. The next day, she did this all over again.

One night, someone took the coins. When the woman came and saw what had happened, she went wild with anger. A curious man heard her and asked what was wrong.

“Someone robbed me, and now my gold is gone. It's money down the drain!” shouted the woman.

“Why was your gold buried in the earth? If it's there, you can't spend it,” said the man.

The woman answered, “I would never spend my gold.”

The man threw a stone into the deep hole. “Bury this then,” he said. “It's worth just as much. Wealth has no value if it's never used.”
